subject: Residency & retention evidence + erasures playbook

Subject: Request: residency evidence + deletion timelines for Hosted API

Sergio,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team ran a quick internal gap analysis and asked for a concise package showing:
- Where Helix tenant data would physically reside for a hosted deployment (region options)
- Retention timelines (including cache / KV TTLs) and exact steps to trigger a tenant-wide erase
- Expected timeline for permanent deletion from backups and replicas
- Any certificates/attestations you can share for the above

Can you send a short written response and any evidence bundle we can upload to our intake system? We need this for our procurement review (target: sign-off by 2027-01-10).

Helix Health
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-17T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: residency evidence + deletion timelines for Hosted API

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Below is a compact package for your intake system; I attached a bundled evidence zip and our erase playbook PDF. If you want I can also drop the same artifacts into the Helix dataroom link (see below).

Quick answers (high-level):
1) Residency (hosted):
   - Default: customer data stored in the region selected at account creation (US-West, US-East, EU-West).
   - Option: We can pin tenant storage to a specific sub-region on Dedicated requests; hosted customers get per-region tenancy.

2) Retention:
   - Active request/response payloads: ephemeral by default; we retain request metadata and logs for 30 days for troubleshooting (configurable up to 90 days by contract).
   - Model input/outputs: not persisted beyond request unless customer opts in to Logging/Diagnostics; if enabled, retention follows tenant settings (30/90/365 days).
   - KV/prefix caches: TTL-based, default 24 hours for ephemeral cache entries; explicit delete will expire cache entries immediately (best-effort).

3) Deletion / erasure workflow (tenant-wide):
   - Trigger: customer support or account owner submits a formal erase request via Console or signed Doc (DocuSign link included).
   - Steps: a) mark tenant for erasure -> b) remove persistent logs & stored artifacts -> c) invalidate caches and rotate keys -> d) scrub from primary storage -> e) enqueue deletion from replicas/backups.
   - Audit evidence: we produce an erasure report listing objects removed and timestamps; provided within 24 hours of completed operation.

4) Backups & replicas:
   - Snapshots/replicas are retained for up to 90 days by default; deletion from backups is asynchronous and completed within 90 days of erase request (we provide manifest entries for each snapshot that is removed).

5) Time-to-complete expectations:
   - Primary data removal from active storage: typically complete within 24–72 hours depending on data volume.
   - Complete purge from backups and geo-replicas: up to 90 days (documented exception window).

Attached: residency-evidence-bundle.zip (contains storage architecture diagram, region mapping, SOC2 section highlights) and erase-playbook-v1.2.pdf (playbook + checklist).

Next steps: If you want faster backup purge SLAs we can propose a contractual commitment (e.g., 30-day backup purge) as an addendum — I copied Kimberly to outline technical feasibility and rollback constraints.

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Elena — quick technical clarifications to augment Sergio's summary: please see the bolded clarifications below and the small table in the attached playbook (erase-playbook-v1.2.pdf).

- Active request payloads: by default we do not write model I/O to persistent object stores. If your integration calls "store_interaction=true" (a customer-configurable flag) those artifacts are placed in tenant-scoped object storage and inherit retention settings.
- Cache mechanics: server-side KV cache is LRU + TTL. An explicit tenant erase nulls cache logical keys immediately; physical cache entries are eligible for GC immediately but may persist in memory briefly until GC cycle completes (usually minutes).
- Backups: our snapshot cadence is daily for production tiers. Snapshots are immutable; removal requires snapshot-level deletion requests. We log snapshot deletions and include those logs in the erasure report.
- Audit logs & attestations: SOC 2 summary and the storage diagram are in the bundle. For stronger evidence we can provide an export of the erasure report (CSV) and a signed attestation of deletion completion.

If Helix requires an accelerated backup purge (e.g., contractually guaranteed 30 days), we can support that on Dedicated or as a hosted add-on with an operational surcharge. Happy to map that to pricing if you'd like.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Security, Redwood Inference
